content: The metabolism of fosaprepitant is significantly influenced by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, leading to various drug interactions. Below are the detailed interactions and recommendations for monitoring or adjusting therapy when fosaprepitant is co-administered with other medications: 1. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors: Exercise caution and monitor closely when fosaprepitant is used with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, as these can increase the levels or effects of fosaprepitant. 2. Cabozantinib: Fosaprepitant increases cabozantinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Cannabidiol: Fosaprepitant increases cannabidiol levels. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Capivasertib: Fosaprepitant increases capivasertib levels. Reduce the capivasertib dose if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 5. Carbamazepine: Fosaprepitant increases carbamazepine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor plasma levels closely. 6. Cenobamate: Cenobamate decreases fosaprepitant levels. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. 7. Cilostazol: Fosaprepitant increases cilostazol levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Cinacalcet: Fosaprepitant increases cinacalcet levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Clomipramine: Fosaprepitant increases clomipramine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Clopidogrel: Fosaprepitant decreases clopidogrel bioactivation by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Clozapine: Fosaprepitant increases clozapine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Conivaptan: Fosaprepitant increases conivaptan levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Conjugated estrogens (oral and vaginal): Fosaprepitant increases the levels of conjugated estrogens. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 14.
